`ggml_metal_graph_compute` into host encode+commit time vs GPU execute+sync
time) showed the 1068-node talker step is **encode 2-3 ms, GPU-execute
38-42 ms** — GPU-execution-bound. Sched-free dispatch or an MTLIndirectCommand
Buffer replay can only remove *host* encode time, so they can't help here (same
verdict as the §210 granite ICB probe). Confirmed empirically: the sched-free
bucket path computes in ~56 ms/step vs ~54 ms dynamic. The op profile explains
the floor — ~460 real ops/step, `mul_mat` only ~24 %, ~85 `cont` copies plus
hundreds of tiny norm/add/rope kernels; it's death by kernel *count*, and the
only lever left is node-count slimming inside the shared `core_attn::kv_self_
attn` (30+ backends, high regression risk) → deprioritized with data instead of
attempted.

Two reusable rules:
- **Attribute host vs device before choosing a dispatch optimization.** "It's
  slow and it's a small model" does NOT mean it's dispatch-bound. If GPU-execute
  dominates, no amount of gallocr/ICB/graph-reuse cleverness moves it; you need
  fewer/bigger kernels, not fewer dispatches.
- **A GPU benchmark taken under contention is noise.** On this 16 GB M1 with
  other sessions running, `CRISPASR_METAL_PROFILE` `gpu_us` for *identical*
  193-node code-pred graphs swung 4-17 ms purely from WindowServer/browser GPU
  time-slicing, and whole-pipeline ms/frame swung 2-3× run to run. Every number
  above was taken load-gated (1-min loadavg < 6, sustained across two checks) or
  as min-of-N interleaved reps. A "3× speedup" measured against a contended
  baseline can be entirely the baseline degrading — interleave old/new in the
  same quiet window before believing a ratio.


## Before starting a "top-priority, profiled" perf target: check whether it's already been tried-and-rejected, and whether a parallel session owns it (§235 triage, 2026-07-11)

Picking the next optimization after the §232 qwen3-tts sweep, the obvious #1 was
PLAN §232's own top item: "port the Parakeet/Nemotron transducer decoder to GPU"
— the decode loop demonstrably runs on host `cblas_sgemv/sgemm`, and the profile
gap vs a competitor was 12-19×. It is a **trap**, and two cheap checks caught it
before any code:

1. **`git log --grep` for prior attempts.** A parallel session had already tried
   it and recorded the result: batched/GPU transducer decode is **5-9× SLOWER**
   (`d0bb4601`, `3fcd5ff3`). A transducer decode step is a handful of tiny
   matmuls (LSTM predictor + joint) with a host↔device sync every step; that is
   precisely the regime where CPU `cblas` beats the GPU (the same lesson as
   qwen3-tts CP_DIRECT being 2× *slower* on CPU, and f5/native-on-GPU losing to
   custom-op-on-CPU). A big *paper* FLOP win on a fine-grained decode loop
   routinely goes **negative** once per-step launch + sync dominate. So: a
   PLAN item marked "[HIGH] 12-19×" is a hypothesis, not a fact — grep for
   whether someone already measured it.
2. **`git worktree list` + recent `git log` for ownership.** The next candidate
   (Moonshine encoder im2col) was being actively worked in another session's
   worktree (`moonshine-decode-stash`); starting it would have collided. On a
   box with many concurrent Claude sessions all pushing to `main`, check who's
   on a target before opening a worktree for it.

The general rule: treat a profiled "top priority" as a lead to *verify*, not a
task to start. `git log --grep`/`--oneline` and `git worktree list` are 10-second
checks that turn "I nearly reimplemented a measured-negative optimization" into
"crossed off with evidence." Record the dead end in PLAN so the next person
doesn't re-derive it (the transducer GPU port is now explicitly marked DEAD in
§235, not silently left as a tempting [HIGH] in §232).


## CosyVoice3 CFM Euler steps: 6 is the sweet spot, and validate it with log-mel corr vs full-steps — NOT ASR roundtrip (§235, 2026-07-11)

Flow-matching CFM trajectories are nearly straight, so an N-step Euler solve
barely differs from a 10-step one down to surprisingly small N — the same
property that let chatterbox drop its S3Gen CFM default 10→6 (§207). Confirmed
for CosyVoice3's DiT-CFM (the single biggest CV3 cost, ~48 % of the wall):
`COSYVOICE3_FLOW_STEPS` swept 10/8/6/4 with a **fixed seed** (identical LM
speech tokens + init noise, so step count is the ONLY variable), quality read
as **log-mel-spectrogram correlation vs the 10-step output** — corr
8→0.9948, 6→0.9925, 4→0.9895. 6 steps is the sweet spot (≥0.98 parity, ASR
verbatim), ~−40 % flow work ≈ −19 % of the wall.

Two transferable methodology points, both learned the hard way this session:
- **ASR roundtrip cannot grade CFM step count.** It was verbatim at 10/8/6 and
  only slipped one word ("brown"→"bound") at 4 — long after the mel-corr starts
  drifting. ASR proves intelligibility, not fidelity; use log-mel corr vs the
  full-step render as the quality axis (chatterbox §207 established this; I
  re-derived it after an ASR-only sweep would have called 4 steps "fine").
- **Calibrate the spectral metric to the accepted threshold.** A raw
  linear-frequency **log-STFT** corr over-weights high-frequency detail (where
  under-stepping shows up) and read 0.958 at 8 steps — falsely alarming;
  the **log-mel** version (n_mels=80) read 0.9948 for the same audio, matching
  chatterbox's 0.98 parity threshold. Match the reference metric before
  applying its threshold, or the numbers don't transfer.
- **The whole-utterance corr under-weights localized artifacts.** At 4 steps
  corr was still 0.9895 (above 0.98) yet ASR misheard a word — the artifact was
  local and the utterance-averaged corr washed it out. When corr and a
  token-level signal disagree near the boundary, trust the more sensitive one
  and stop there. Final arbiter for any quality-affecting DEFAULT remains a
  human listen on 2–3 diverse sentences — recommend, don't unilaterally flip.

## A "GPU" model can be silently running on CPU — audit for hot graphs pinned to backend_cpu and CLI adapters that never forward use_gpu (f5-tts / moonshine, 2026-07-11)

Two backends looked like they "supported GPU" but never used it, and both cost
real time before anyone noticed:

- **moonshine**: the CLI adapter zero-initialized `moonshine_init_params` and
  never set `use_gpu`, so every run — *including the §232 Kaggle "GPU"
  benchmarks* — used the CPU backend. The whole "moonshine encoder is 6-21×
  slower than transcribe.cpp" investigation was chasing a CPU-vs-GPU comparison
  mislabeled as GPU-vs-GPU. One line (`mp.use_gpu = params.use_gpu`) → encoder
  4-6× faster on Metal. The tell: the model-load banner lacked its `(GPU)`
  suffix and `CRISPASR_METAL_PROFILE=1` printed zero `[metal-prof]` lines.
- **f5-tts**: the DiT graph (the dominant compute) was hardcoded
  `ggml_backend_graph_compute(ctx->backend_cpu, gf)` with the gallocr bound to
  backend_cpu's buffer type, regardless of `use_gpu`. Weights loaded on
  `ctx->backend` (GPU), so on Metal it *worked* — unified memory let the CPU
  backend read the GPU-resident weights — and just ran every forward on the CPU
  (sampling showed `ggml_vec_dot_f16_f32` / flash-attn in libggml-cpu). Compute
  on `ctx->backend` instead (== backend_cpu when use_gpu is off) → 7.8×/step.

**Audit recipe when a backend feels slow on GPU:** grep for
`ggml_backend_graph_compute(.*_cpu` and `gallocr_new(...buffer_type(.*_cpu` in
the hot path; check the CLI adapter actually forwards `params.use_gpu`; confirm
the load banner says `(GPU)` and `CRISPASR_METAL_PROFILE` emits per-graph lines.
On unified-memory Metal a CPU-pinned graph never errors — it silently computes
on the CPU while claiming the GPU backend.

Corollary — **low-step "degenerate on both CPU and GPU" is not automatically a
quality floor.** f5 produced garbage at 4 steps on *both* backends; the first
read was "4 steps is below the model's floor." It was actually a shared bug:
`pos_in` set once but the gallocr re-aliased its slot every step, corrupting
RoPE positions from step 1 (the omnivoice §245 input-aliasing class). Fixing it
made 16-step output roundtrip verbatim. When both backends agree on garbage,
suspect a shared bug before blaming the step count.

## Micro-optimizing an already-BLAS'd path with a GPU-ggml port is usually a dud — check for existing Accelerate/cblas and measure encode-vs-execute BEFORE porting (f5 / titanet perf sweep, 2026-07-11)

After the f5 base fix (7.8×, a real *bug*), the "obvious" follow-on GPU
optimizations were all measured duds, and the pattern is worth internalizing:

- **f5 batched CFG** (run the 2 CFG DiT passes as one B=2 graph): implemented,
  correct (corr 1.00000 vs sequential, 4D-RoPE + batched flash-attn work on
  Metal) — but NO speedup. The Metal profile (979-node DiT, ~1.5 ms host-encode
  vs ~1-2 s GPU-execute/forward) proved it's compute-bound, so B=2 just doubles
  per-dispatch work. Batching only helps *dispatch*-bound graphs.
- **f5 F16 activations** (cast QKV/FFN matmul inputs to F16): correct, but
  slightly *slower* (added cast nodes) → the DiT isn't matmul-bound either. The
  ~0.8-1 s/forward is the ~800 small ops + flash-attn, which neither lever hits.
- **f5 host input-embed → GPU** and **titanet GPU port**: both already run on
  **Accelerate BLAS** (`cblas_sgemm`) on CPU. titanet's *default* path is legacy
  Accelerate (~1 s/forward); its ggml-CPU path is 1.7× *slower*, so a GPU-ggml
  port would have to beat Accelerate with a graph that already loses to it.

The durable rule: **the big wins are bugs, not micro-opts.** Before porting a
hot path to the GPU, (1) check whether it's already `cblas`/Accelerate-optimized
— if so a naive ggml graph often loses; (2) split host-encode vs GPU-execute to
know if you're dispatch- or compute-bound — batching and precision changes only
help the former. Guess-and-check across an already-optimized seam burns hours
for nothing; a per-op Metal capture is the only honest next step there.

27. **VoiceDesign == different model, not just + caption encoder.** Irodori-TTS
600M-v3-VoiceDesign has completely different dimensions from the base v3 500M
(model_dim 1280 vs 2048, latent_dim 32 vs 128, text_dim 512 vs 1280, 12 vs 24
DiT layers, llm-jp-3-150m tokenizer vs sarashina2.2). The converter/runtime
already read hparams from config/GGUF dynamically, so the dimension changes were
handled — but the assumption that "VoiceDesign = base + caption" would have led
to hardcoded wrong dimensions. Always check the actual checkpoint config.

### #81: profile per-node before trusting a handover's bottleneck theory — the "memory traffic" was two F16 matmuls the quantizer silently skipped

The FastConformer CPU-perf handover attributed the 1.5× gap vs onnx-asr to
ggml's per-op intermediate materialization and proposed cont-reduction /
gallocr / fusion work. A 30-line sched-eval-callback profiler
(`CRISPASR_FC_PROFILE=1`, aggregate by op+shape) showed conts+casts ≈ 3%,
sched ≈ 1% — and **35% of encoder time in `conv.pw1/pw2` F16 matmuls**.
The converter writes those as 3D conv tensors `(1, d, N)`; the quantizer's
`ggml_n_dims(t) == 2` rule skips them; so every quantized FastConformer
GGUF shipped with F16 pointwise-conv weights running on ggml's slow
(~6× vs Q8_0) CPU F16 mul_mat path. Three durable lessons:

1. **Grep quantized GGUFs for leftover F16 2D-consumed weights** — a
   tensor stored 3D but consumed as `reshape_2d + mul_mat` is invisible
   to dimension-based quantize rules. Check with
   `GGUFReader` per-tensor types on layer 0, not by assuming "q8_0 model".
   Fixed at both ends: `crispasr-quantize` now quantizes
   `*.conv.pw[12].weight` as its 2D view; runtimes repack old GGUFs at
   load (`core_conformer::repack_conv_pw_q8`, `CRISPASR_FC_PW_Q8`).
2. **ggml CPU F16 mul_mat is a perf trap** (~30 GFLOP/s vs ~176 for q8_0
   on M1) — same class as the F16-cast-per-graph conv trap (§conv1d
   hygiene), but for matmul weights.
3. **`GGML_BLAS=ON` does nothing for a backend whose sched only registers
   {gpu, cpu}** — the blas backend must be in the sched's backend list to
   ever be scheduled. The VPS "OpenBLAS build" benchmarks never used it
   in the FastConformer path.

Bonus (bit-identical, gated): fused QKV (`CRISPASR_FC_FUSED_QKV`, one
matmul + view-split; concat weights at load) and strided
`flash_attn_ext` inputs (drop Q/K/V `ggml_cont`s; `CRISPASR_FC_ATTN_CONT=1`
restores). Verified bit-identical on the full CTC logit grid — view-split
matmul and strided flash reads change nothing numerically. Combined:
parakeet-ctc q8_0 M1 CPU 1.13→0.73 s (re-quantized GGUF: 0.60 s, 18.4× RT).

### #81 GPU phase: a finite attention mask constant is not a mask — pad garbage overruns it a few blocks deep

Building the bucketed-padding path (pad T to a bucket, mask pad frames)
for the FastConformer encoder produced transcripts that matched but
logits that drifted ~0.7 — and the drift ENTERED at block 3, not block 0
(bisected with `CRISPASR_FC_MAX_LAYERS=N` truncation). Three lessons:

1. **Mask pad KEYS with `-INFINITY`, never `-1e9`.** Pad columns carry
   untrained garbage that grows across blocks; by block ~3 their QK
   scores reach 1e8+ and a finite mask constant no longer dominates —
   pad keys get real softmax weight. `-inf + finite = -inf` always.
   (`make_local_attn_mask`'s -1e9 is fine for its use — masked positions
   there hold trained-scale values.) Also re-zero pad columns at every
   block boundary so 0-weight × huge-value artifacts can't arise.
2. **Bitwise equality across different tensor shapes is bounded by
   size-adaptive GEMM kernel selection.** After fixing every structural
   leak (attention keys, dw-conv inputs, pre-encode stage boundaries),
   a rel≈3e-9 seed remained at the pre-encode matmuls: im2col GEMMs pick
   different micro-kernels for different widths, regrouping the same dot
   products (ULP reassociation), and 24 LayerNorms amplify it to ~0.7 in
   logits. Same accepted class as BLAS-variant drift — acceptance is
   identical decoded output, and bit-equality only when shapes coincide.
   Corollary: when a "leak" survives every masking fix, check whether
   the first divergence is ULP-sized before hunting more structure.
3. **Build worktrees with ABSOLUTE paths** (`cmake --build $W/build`).
   A shell cwd reset mid-session sent two rebuilds into the main tree's
   build dir; the stale worktree dylib then "disproved" a correct fix
   (same max_abs before/after). `strings <dylib> | grep <new-env-var>`
   is the 5-second staleness check.

### #81 endgame: three more durable lessons from the fleet requant + CUDA phase

1. **A documented op-fallback note is an unexploited perf bug.** The
   `fattn.cu` per-head-mask guard (`mask->ne[2] != 1` → flash rejected on
   CUDA) had been sitting in PERFORMANCE.md's CUDA op-support table since
   May as "the dominant CPU-fallback" — acting on it (manual QK^T +
   soft_max_ext attention, all-GPU) was a **3.2×** on long audio. When a
   support-table entry says "falls back to CPU on <backend>", treat it as
   an open perf ticket: either restructure the graph around the guard or
   fix the kernel upstream. `GGML_SCHED_DEBUG=2` per backend per GPU is
   the audit tool.
2. **Requantizing an old GGUF with today's quantizer is NOT identity —
   rules drift.** Old parakeet q4_k files kept the whole transducer head
   (decoder.embed, joint.out, joint.pred) at F16 under rules that no
   longer exist; a naive re-quant silently changes those tensors too. The
   safe fleet-fix pattern: same-type tensors byte-copy (so requant = the
   minimal intended diff), a structural gate that refuses ANY unexpected
   type/data change, per-file `--tensor-type` pins to reproduce retired
   rules, and strict transcript equality (old + runtime repack vs new)
   as acceptance. The gate caught both the rules drift AND a
   down-quantization bug (q8 pw → q4 on re-runs) before anything shipped.
3. **`HfApi.upload_file` can strand after its commit lands (CLOSE_WAIT)
   on Kaggle too** — not just on the Mac (memory said laptop-specific;
   wrong). A single-threaded pipeline wedges forever on one call. Pattern:
   run HF network ops on daemon threads with a join timeout, then verify
   server-side (list_repo_tree size match) and treat a hung-but-landed
   upload as success. Progress mirroring to a side repo (small JSON per
   file) is what makes a wedged cloud kernel diagnosable at all.

## Exact greedy code-parity is unachievable for a QUANTIZED AR audio LM — confirm the port with a step-0 logit-rank probe, not byte-exact codes (MOSS-TTS-v1.5 #249, 2026-07-13)

Greedy code-parity (C++ Q4_K vs the HF BF16 reference, temps=0) for the moss-tts
backbone matched only ~0.5% of frames and diverged from **frame 0** — which looked
alarming but is exactly what a correct port produces here. Two findings, one a real
bug and one an intrinsic limit:

1. **Real bug (fixed): tokenizer newline grouping.** The prompt tokenizer cloned
   from `qwen3_asr` used a crude whitespace pre-splitter that split `>` from a
   trailing `\n`. Qwen's pre-tokenizer regex `[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n]*` groups
   punctuation with trailing newlines (`>\n`=397, `):\n`=982, `:\n`=510). A
   dedicated `moss-tts-promptdiff` kernel isolated it: the prompt TEXT was
   identical, only the tokenization of newlines differed (first mismatch at the
   first `>\n`). Fix = a proper Qwen2/3 pre-tokenizer (`mt_qwen_pretokenize`,
   contractions | prefix+letters | digit | punct+trailing-nl | ws+nl | ws). After
   it the 67-token conditioning prompt is **byte-identical** to the HF processor
   (`first_mismatch=null`). **Gate 0 for any text→audio LM: diff the col-0 prompt
   ids against the HF processor and require byte-identity BEFORE looking at codes.**

2. **Intrinsic (not a bug): quantization near-tie onset flip + AR chaos.** Even
   with byte-identical prompts the codes diverge from the very first token. The
   decisive `moss-tts-logit0` probe (`moss_tts_debug_first_audio_logits` — prefill
   the prompt, dump head-0 logits, no 8B reference, no F16 download) showed the
   reference's greedy pick (code 143) is the C++ Q4_K distribution's **rank-1
   runner-up**, only **0.135 logits** below the C++ argmax (1021). Q4_K rounding
   (O(0.1–0.5) on logits) flips this near-tie. Because the MOSS delay makes every
   un-delayed frame span many raw AR steps, one flip cascades: ~n_vq·T greedy
   decisions at even 99.9% per-decision agreement → ~0.1% joint survival, i.e. the
   0.5% observed. Codebook-0 (coarse RVQ) still re-syncs to exact reference values
   at scattered frames (807, 578, 756; 2-frame-shifted runs 400/575/254) — the
   models produce the same coarse audio, differing only on quant-sensitive fine
   residuals. **This extends the F16 voxtral-tts lesson (exact at frame 0, diverges
   by frame ~7) to the QUANTIZED case where even frame 0 flips** — and the
   logit-rank probe is what distinguishes an expected near-tie flip (rank ≤1–2,
   gap <~1 logit) from a real head/numerics bug (ref pick far down). The only
   acceptance gate for a quantized AR audio LM is the ASR round-trip (HARD RULE #3),
   never byte-exact greedy codes.

**Voice cloning (same port) validated the encoder path the cheap way too:** a
self-contained closed-loop kernel (`tools/kaggle/moss-tts-voiceclone`) — synth a
reference clip R, clone its voice onto a new sentence C (`--voice R
--i-have-rights`), and a no-voice baseline B — gates on (a) `--voice` runs clean +
non-silent, (b) ASR(C) reproduces the clone text, (c) speaker-embedding
cosine(C,R) > cosine(B,R) via Resemblyzer. Result on Q4_K: cos 0.845 vs 0.585
(Δ+0.26) with the words preserved. Harness gotcha: the crispasr whisper CLI
interleaves device/model-load noise (and an appended "generated by artificial
intelligence" disclosure) on the transcript lines — feed the FULL ANSI-stripped
stdout to a word-OVERLAP check (present-in, not exact-match); a `[-400:]` tail
truncation dropped the real transcript and faked a FAIL.

## A GPU-vs-reference RTF gap that survives kernel parity is per-step HOST detours — fuse them into the step graph; unified-memory Metal hides exactly this class of cost (omnivoice #254, 2026-07-16)

After single-shot synthesis landed, omnivoice on the reporter's RTX 5070 Ti was
still RTF 0.17 vs omnivoice.cpp's 0.144 — with the forward kernels already at
parity (~34 ms/step both). The residual was entirely between the forwards, on
the host, per MaskGIT step: (a) audio-embedding lookup via a separate get_rows
graph with an ~18 MB F32 readback, a single-threaded codebook sum, and a ~5 MB
re-upload of the summed embeds; (b) a full-sequence logits readback (~39 MB,
out_dim×T_c) when only the target slice is consumed; (c) single-threaded
triple-log-softmax CFG scoring (~13M `exp` per step); (d) multi-MB per-step
vector allocs incl. a full 18 MB `u_logits` copy in the interval-CFG path.
~44 ms/step of pure host work next to a 27 ms forward.

**The fix — fused step graph** (`OMNIVOICE_FUSED_STEP`): the shifted audio-token
ids (140 KB of int32) are the ONLY per-step upload. In-graph: get_rows +
codebook sum + concat with a device-resident text-embedding tensor (uploaded
once into its OWN backend buffer — gallocr-managed tensors get aliased, a
dedicated buffer is exempt); after the transformer, `ggml_cont` views emit ONLY
the target logit slices. CFG scoring threads over target positions. Verdict on
the reporter's box: gen 3.55 s → 1.53 s (2.3×), RTF 0.07 — ~2× faster than
omnivoice.cpp — and ONE CUDA-graph warmup for all 32 steps.

Durable techniques from the byte-identity requirement (codes cmp-identical to
the legacy path on M1 Metal across 2-forward / unified / interval-CFG K=2 /
guidance=0, AND on the reporter's CUDA box):

1. **In-graph embedding sums can be bitwise-equal to a host sum** if the add
   ORDER matches: chained `ggml_add` over per-codebook views in cb-ascending
   order reproduces the host `dst[j] += src[j]` loop exactly (elementwise F32
   IEEE add, no reassociation). Order-matched graph math is what turns a perf
   rewrite into a cmp-verifiable no-op.
2. **Threading a sampling loop without changing output:** draw the Gumbel noise
   SERIALLY first (same rng object, same t-outer/cb-inner order as the serial
   loop), then consume the precomputed array from worker threads. The rng
   stream — and thus the output — is bit-identical. Data-dependent draw counts
   (class_temp>0 top-k sampling) can't be precomputed → that path stays serial.
3. **Platform asymmetry: judge host-detour optimizations on a DISCRETE-GPU
   box.** On M1 the same change is NEUTRAL (matched-load per-stage A/B: 96.3 s
   fused vs 93.7 s legacy for the same paragraph; legacy's embed prep cost 0.9 s
   of ~94 s) because unified memory makes the readback/re-upload nearly free
   and Accelerate eats the sums. The 2.3× only exists where host↔device
   round-trips and single-thread scoring are real costs. Inverse of the usual
   lesson: this time the M1 could not SHOW the win, not fake one.
4. **ggml fork CUDA-graph facts** (checked in `ggml-cuda.cu`): capture state is
   keyed PER cgraph (`ggml_cuda_graph_get_key` = nodes[0]), so several
   alternating persistent graphs each keep their own capture — alternation is
   NOT the enemy, per-step REBUILD is. And `TAG_GET_ROWS_CUDA_GRAPHS` disables
   capture for any graph containing GET_ROWS on a *quantized* table (host sync
   in the kquant path) — omnivoice survives because the quantizer keeps
   audio_embd/audio_output/llm.token_embd at F16. Audit the embd dtype BEFORE
   fusing embedding lookups into a forward graph on another backend.
5. **Reference-voice disk cache** (reporter parity ask, shipped as
   `CRISPASR_OMNIVOICE_VOICE_CACHE`): the RVQ ref encode is deterministic →
   cache content-addressed (FNV-1a over the PREPROCESSED pcm + an
   encoder-weight fingerprint), OVC1 header + int32 codes, atomic tmp+rename,
   same dir resolution as the pocket_tts latents cache. Second run loads in
   ~0 ms; audio data chunk bit-identical (only the timestamped C2PA chunk
   differs — compare WAV `data` chunks, not whole files).

Bench-hygiene reminders this session re-taught: a loaded shared M1 (loadavg
100–290) inverted the Metal A/B verdict TWICE before matched-load per-stage
medians settled it (the tell: the arms' identical decode code differing 3.8×);
and `curl -C -` resume on top of a 29-byte HTML error stub produces a
GGUF-with-garbage-prefix that parses as `invalid magic 'Inva'` — delete before
retrying, never resume a file you haven't validated.

## `git apply --3way` STAGES its result — a later `git add X && git commit` sweeps it up

Applying a patch with `git apply --3way` leaves the result **staged**, not just
in the working tree. So a subsequent `git add <unrelated files> && git commit`
commits the patch too, under a message that says nothing about it. That is how
the `group_words_into_speaker_runs` diarize DRY refactor landed inside
`29e3e7af6`, a commit labelled "mel-band-roformer reference dumper" — and it
was pushed to shared `main` before its unit tests had been run (they pass:
21/21, including the pre-existing `apply_pyannote` / `score_speaker_for_range`
cases, which is what makes the refactor provably behaviour-preserving — but the
verification happened in the wrong order).

Habits: after `git apply --3way`, run `git status` and either commit the patch
deliberately on its own or `git restore --staged` the parts you are not ready
to ship; and prefer `git commit <explicit paths>` over `git add X && git commit`
when the tree holds more than one logical change. On a repo with concurrent
sessions pushing to `main`, the mistake is not fixable by amending — history is
already shared — so the correction has to be additive, like this note.

The refactor itself is real and worth knowing about: the word→speaker-run
grouping + short-run stability fold used by the pyannote/sherpa segment
splitters now lives in one pure, unit-testable helper,
`crispasr_diarize_internal::group_words_into_speaker_runs()`
(`src/crispasr_diarize.cpp` / `_internal.h`), instead of being duplicated per
splitter. `min_run_cs <= 0` disables the fold (split on every speaker change);
50 cs is the pyannote default that suppresses one-word track-index flips.

## A normalization stage amplifies upstream float error — input-align it before trusting its cos (§248 MBR)

Mel-Band RoFormer's `band_split` starts with RMSNorm
(`F.normalize(x,-1)*sqrt(dim)*gamma`). Diffing `band_split_out` off OUR STFT
scored cos=0.976 and looked like a port bug — but the band_split MATH was
already proven exact (an identical numpy recompute from the fixture's own
`band_gathered` matched to cos=1.0). Cause: RMSNorm divides by each band's L2
norm, so on near-silent bands it amplifies the ~5e-4 float-level difference
between our radix-2 FFT and torch's STFT into a large relative error. Measured:
a *uniform* ±5e-4 perturbation on `band_gathered` alone tanks band_split to
cos 0.73 (our real, correlated error did better at 0.976).

Lesson (a sharper form of "gate input alignment before trusting per-layer cos"):
when a stage BEGINS with a normalization (RMS/Layer/L2), a cos taken off your
own upstream output conflates two things — your stage's correctness and the
upstream's float rounding, magnified. Diff that stage fed the REFERENCE's input
tensor, so it tests only its own math; validate the upstream separately by its
own pre-norm stage (here stft_packed, cos=1.0). After input-aligning,
band_split_out was cos=1.000000 (max_abs 1.5e-3 = f16 weight rounding). The
same input-alignment applies to every later MBR stage (each RoFormer block also
opens with RMSNorm). General rule for the harness: prefer feeding each stage the
reference input over chaining your own outputs, whenever the stage's first op is
scale-sensitive.


## CI has no NVIDIA GPU — a CUDA-only graph path (mimo RVQ) is guarded by an on-Kaggle exact-parity smoke, not CI (#309)

`perf(mimo-tokenizer): move RVQ to CUDA` (#309) runs MiMo's 8-stage Euclidean
RVQ inside the encoder graph when the tokenizer weights are CUDA-resident:
`scores = 2*(e·x) - ||e||^2` (mul_mat + scale + sub of precomputed codebook
norms) -> `argmax` (== `argmin ||x-e||^2`) -> `get_rows` residual. The argmax
output is contiguous, so it sidesteps the CUDA `get_rows` non-contiguous-index
abort; `mul_mat_set_prec(F32)` keeps the dot products exact.

The catch: the release CI matrix (linux-x86_64, linux-vulkan, macos, wasm, ios,
android) has NO NVIDIA GPU, so the whole `#if defined(GGML_USE_CUDA)` RVQ branch
COMPILES but never EXECUTES in CI. A green CI is necessary but NOT sufficient for
this path. Its regression guard is the model smoke tool's exact CPU/CUDA compare,
run on a CUDA box (Kaggle):

```
CRISPASR_MIMO_SMOKE_GPU=1 CRISPASR_MIMO_TOK_VERIFY_RVQ=1 \
    ./mimo-tokenizer-smoke mimo-tokenizer-q4_k.gguf samples/jfk.wav
# -> [ ok ] rvq_cpu_gpu_compare  codes=2208 mismatches=0
```

Validated on an RTX 2080 Ti: 2,208 codes, 0 mismatches, 5.65x faster than the CPU
fallback. Any future edit to the RVQ or encoder graph must re-run this on real
CUDA — do not trust CI alone. Rollback / diagnosis: `CRISPASR_MIMO_TOK_CPU_RVQ=1`
forces the CPU argmin path. (General rule: whenever a perf change adds a
`GGML_USE_CUDA`-gated compute path, name its Kaggle parity check in the PR, since
CI cannot cover it — same lesson as the parakeet/nemotron ggml-decode A/Bs.)


## "Backend miscomputes my pipeline" ≠ "op X is broken": arbitrate with test-backend-ops, and beware aggregate precision (#304 native-Vulkan post-mortem)

CosyVoice3 produces noise on the Vulkan backend (the shipped fix CPU-routes it).
Chasing "make it run natively on Vulkan," a chain of app-level symptoms kept
pointing at a broken op — and kept being WRONG until ggml's own unit tests
settled it. The sequence, and the lessons:

1. **LM is fine, flow/HiFT are not.** With `CRISPASR_COSYVOICE3_GREEDY=1` (forces
   argmax so two backends yield identical tokens iff their logits agree) the LM
   matched CPU **512/512 tokens** on both MoltenVK and a real Tesla P100 — but the
   flow mel diverged (cosine(cpu,vk)=**0.961**, max element diff 6.78). *Greedy is
   the tool for cross-backend determinism*: sampling hides a miscompute behind a
   "different but valid" sequence; argmax exposes it.

2. **"Healthy stats ≠ correct" (again — cf. the F5/HARD-RULE token-parity lesson).**
   The Vulkan flow mel had a perfectly healthy RANGE (min/max/rms like CPU, no
   NaN), so an early read said "flow works, HiFT is the breaker." False: a
   HiFT-on-CPU hybrid fed that mel still produced noise. A healthy-looking
   intermediate can be wrong in CONTENT. Only an element-wise cos/max-diff vs a
   reference (same input) is trustworthy — dump raw tensors, not summaries.

3. **Isolate DISPATCH from OP.** Suspecting my own single-backend `gallocr`
   dispatch (gallocr reuses input buffers as scratch — a real footgun for
   multi-step graphs), I added `CRISPASR_COSYVOICE3_FORCE_GALLOCR=1` to run the
   gallocr path on the CPU backend and diff it against the CPU scheduler: **cosine
   1.000000, max diff 0 — bit-identical.** The dispatch was never the bug.

4. **The arbiter: ggml's own `test-backend-ops` on the target backend.** Built it
   with `GGML_VULKAN=ON` and ran it on a real P100 (Kaggle). EVERY op the flow +
   HiFT touch PASSES vs the CPU reference — IM2COL 88/88, CONV_TRANSPOSE_1D,
   MUL_MAT 892/892, NORM(LayerNorm) 10/10, RMS_NORM, SOFT_MAX 212/212, GELU/SILU,
   ROPE 288/288, CONCAT/GET_ROWS/CPY/PAD, all `Backend Vulkan0: OK`. There is **no
   broken op.** My successive "it's the conv" / "it's LayerNorm" hypotheses were
   all disproven by the op the primitive's own unit test. LESSON: before claiming
   "ggml op X miscomputes on backend Y," RUN test-backend-ops for X on Y — it is
   cheap, authoritative, and app-independent. An app-level divergence is evidence
   of a *problem*, never of a *specific op*.

5. **Root cause = aggregate numerical sensitivity, not a bug.** All ops pass
   *within tolerance*, but Vulkan is not bit-exact to CPU (fp16-class accumulation
   vs fp32). Those in-tolerance per-op deltas ACCUMULATE across the deep flow (22
   DiT layers × 6 CFM Euler steps) and are amplified by the CFM ODE integration +
   the log-mel HiFT vocoder's sensitivity → audible noise. The LM survives because
   it is shallow-per-token and robust. cosine 0.961 (distributed small error, not
   a localized drop or NaN) is the signature of accumulation, not a broken kernel.
   There is nothing to file upstream and no single op to fix; the all-CPU route
   stays correct. (Corollary: a numerically-sensitive generative head — flow
   matching / diffusion + a log-domain vocoder — may be un-portable to a
   lower-accumulation backend even when every op is individually "correct.")

6. **Process bug worth remembering: a global find-replace can eat a function's own
   body.** Converting ~15 `ggml_backend_sched_*(ctx->sched, gf)` call sites to
   thin `cv3_sched_*(ctx, gf)` shims via a blanket string replace ALSO rewrote the
   `ggml_backend_sched_*` calls INSIDE the shim definitions → the shims called
   themselves → infinite recursion → stack-overflow SIGSEGV on any non-gallocr
   (CPU/Metal) path. It hid because the gallocr branch skipped the recursion, so
   only the "other" backend crashed — and I first misattributed it to a stale
   build. When a blanket replace targets a name, exclude the definitions of the
   wrappers you're routing THROUGH.

## A public API with no caller is a harness-blind zone announcing itself — and an ONNX export may FOLD a BatchNorm your C++ still expects as tensors (#334 CosyVoice3 CAMPPlus, 2026-08-06)

CosyVoice3's WAV voice cloning was reported as "unnatural foreign accent". The
per-stage harness ended at the talker/flow/HiFT and every stage passed. The
speaker embedding — the single tensor that decides *whose voice comes out* —
had no stage at all, and was wrong: **cos 0.737** against `campplus.onnx`.

**The bug.** CAMPPlus ends
`transit3.linear(Conv1d, bias=False) → out_nonlinear(BN + ReLU) → StatsPool`.
An ONNX exporter is free to fold that trailing BatchNorm into the preceding
convolution, and CosyVoice3's export does: the graph carries a bare
`/xvector/out_nonlinear/relu/Relu` with **no BN parameters anywhere**, while
`/xvector/transit3/linear/Conv` gained a fused weight *and a fused bias*
(transit1/transit2 keep named, bias-free weights because no BN follows them).
Our `bn_relu_conv1d` never applied a conv bias, so the fold was silently
dropped and the last 512 channels reached the pooling un-normalised.

Read the checkpoint, don't assume the shape. The three consumers of this same
C++ ship **two different export shapes** — chatterbox and dots.tts keep
`out_nonlinear`'s BN as explicit tensors (and have no transit bias, so the fix
is bit-identical for them); only CosyVoice3 folds. Code written against one
shape had simply never met the other. A GGUF's tensor-name list settles this in
seconds without downloading the file: GGUF puts the tensor table in the header,
so a ranged HTTP read of the first few MB plus a 30-line parser lists every
name in a multi-GB artifact on HuggingFace.

### Three things that let it hide, all reusable

1. **`cosyvoice3_tts_extract_{spk_emb,ref_mel,speech_tokens}` had no caller
   anywhere in the tree.** Three public C APIs, exported, documented, dead. That
   is not a tidiness problem — it is a *measurement* problem: an API nothing
   calls is a computation nothing checks. Grep for callers of the entry points
   your harness is supposed to cover; the ones with zero are your blind zone,
   and they are cheap to find. (Sibling of [[prove the new path executes]]:
   there the path shipped inert, here the *check* was never wired up.)

2. **A value-bijection is not a slot check.** I first "verified" the converter
   by matching all 617 GGUF tensors 1:1 to ONNX initializers *by value* — unique
   match both ways, nothing dropped, nothing duplicated. That proves the weight
   SET is intact and says nothing about which slot each landed in, and it nearly
   ended the investigation. Only the end-to-end embedding comparison found the
   bug — and the bug was not a mis-assignment at all, it was a term the forward
   never applied, which no weight audit could ever have seen.

3. **The ground truth was in the graph the whole time.** The converter assigns
   an anonymous initializer tail (`onnx::Conv_4619`) by hard-coded index plus a
   shape assertion — a guess that a same-shaped neighbour would satisfy. But a
   torch ONNX export keeps the full scope path on the *node*:
   `node.name == '/xvector/block2/tdnnd3/linear1/Conv'`, with the initializer as
   input slot 1 (weight) or 2 (bias). Walk the nodes and every anonymous tensor
   names itself. Prefer that to index arithmetic — and note that slot 2 existing
   at all is exactly the signal that a BN was folded in.

### The diagnostic that pinned it

Guessing which term was wrong would have been slow. Instead: **break the
reference the same way and see if it matches.** Zero the suspect bias in the
ONNX model, re-run, compare to the C++ output — cos **0.999998**, norms 19.937
vs 19.939. That converts "something in a 3000-node network is off" into proof
about one tensor, and it is cheap for any reference you can edit and re-run.
(Fixed: 0.999997 against the unmodified reference.)

### Why it read as "quality", not as a bug

The baked voice bank's embeddings are produced by `campplus.onnx` in Python at
build time, so bank voices were always correct; only the runtime `--voice
ref.wav` path went through the broken code. A wrong-but-plausible 192-d vector
does not crash, does not NaN, and does not look wrong in any summary statistic
— it clones a slightly different person. When a user reports "cloning quality"
and the presets are fine, suspect the runtime-only half of the front end.

## #195 parakeet-ctc-1.1b-ja CTC routing (agent memory `project_195_parakeet_ctc_ja_routing`, migrated 2026-08-06)

---
name: project_195_parakeet_ctc_ja_routing
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 216d15c0-fd99-420f-a88e-61ab2b9d4ad5
---

Issue #195: user (sayou112) got `required tensor 'decoder.embed.weight' not
found` on `cstr/parakeet-ctc-1.1b-ja-GGUF`. **The GGUF was already correct** —
arch `canary-ctc`, CTC head present, 42L/1024d/vocab-4000; verified it
transcribes JA fluently at 4.1× RT via auto-detect. Root cause was purely
wrong-backend: user forced `--backend parakeet` (RNN-T/TDT transducer), and our
HF README *told* them to. A pure-CTC NeMo model (EncDecCTCModelBPE, e.g.
grider-transwithai/parakeet-ctc-1.1b-ja) has NO decoder/joint — it runs on the
**canary_ctc runtime** via `--backend fastconformer-ctc` (or auto-detect).

Key facts:
- **CTC vs transducer split**: `parakeet` backend = transducer (needs
  decoder.embed/lstm + joint.*). Pure-CTC = encoder + `ctc.weight`/`ctc.bias`,
  arch tag `canary-ctc`, backend `fastconformer-ctc` (adapter wraps
  src/canary_ctc.cpp). The AED `canary` backend (src/canary.h) is a DIFFERENT
  model (encoder-decoder w/ beam search) — NOT for CTC GGUFs.
- **Converters**: convert-parakeet-to-gguf.py = transducer only (maps only the
  *hybrid* `ctc_decoder.decoder_layers.0` head, not a pure-CTC
  `decoder.decoder_layers.0`). Pure CTC → convert-stt-fastconformer-ctc-to-gguf.py
  (arch canary-ctc).
- **Latent routing bug fixed (63906515)**: GGUF-arch map had `canary-ctc` →
  `canary` (AED!) and the broad `canary` filename heuristic had the same hazard.
  Fixed → `fastconformer-ctc`; added `canary`+`ctc` filename guard; accept
  `--backend canary-ctc/canary_ctc/fastconformer_ctc` aliases.
- **Also shipped (18121a13)**: parakeet.cpp pure-CTC guard (clean redirect error
  instead of null-tensor wall); convert-parakeet refuses pure-CTC .nemo; HF
  README de-`--backend parakeet`'d + re-uploaded.

Ops note: `/Volumes/backups` (disk5s1) threw I/O errors mid-task and would NOT
remount — did the routing fix in an internal-disk worktree
(/Users/christianstrobele/code/CrispASR-canary-ctc, since removed). See
`feedback_storage_paths`; when the external disk is down, internal /Users had
24GB free (the 99-100%-full note was stale).

## #205 --max-len text-split + granite-plus (agent memory `project_205_maxlen_granite_plus`, migrated 2026-08-06)

Issue #205 (reporter AppleSheeple): `--max-len` had no effect on granite/qwen3
(worked on whisper/cohere). SHIPPED to main `f1ccc0e7`.

**Root cause 1 (the title bug):** `crispasr_make_disp_segments`
(`examples/cli/crispasr_output.cpp`) only split a segment when it carried
word-level timings. granite/qwen3 (and granite-plus in plain mode) return
TEXT-ONLY segments → `--max-len`/`-osrt`/`-ovtt`/`--split-on-punct` were no-ops.
FIX: added a text-splitting path — segment has text but no usable words and
`max_len>0` → greedy word-pack to ≤max_len BYTES (over-long tokens / space-less
CJK broken at UTF-8 codepoint boundaries via `split_long_token`/
`pack_text_to_maxlen`/`split_ws_words`), timestamps interpolated by cumulative
char length; composes with split_on_punct. Word-carrying backends (parakeet,
cohere, whisper-own-path) unchanged.

**Root cause 2 (granite PLUS "transcribing broken") — PROPERLY FIXED main
cbb73892 (#205b):** the plus model's timestamp/SAA instruction made the decoder
loop "thank you thank you …" (garbage). FIRST cut (f1ccc0e7) wrongly concluded the
model's ts-mode is non-functional and gated it OFF (CRISPASR_GRANITE_WORD_TS).
User pushed back ("fix PROPERLY, compare the python blueprints, it worked before").
REAL ROOT CAUSE (from the HF model card prompt + `ref/granite_speech/`): the plus
model needs IBM's CONTROL-TOKEN chat template
(`<|start_of_role|>user<|end_of_role|>…<|end_of_text|><|start_of_role|>assistant…`),
but was routed to the legacy granite-4.0 `USER:/ASSISTANT:` wrapper. Discriminator
`use_v3_template = audio_token_index < 50000` MISSES it because
granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus shares granite-4.0's audio_token_index == **100352**.
Plain transcription survives the wrong wrapper; the demanding ts/SAA instruction
doesn't. KEY diagnostic: at max_new=200 the model emitted correctly-RISING [T:N]
tags (knew the audio DURATION) but "thank you" content → not a long-decode bug,
it's the template. FIX: `use_v3_template = (audio_token_index < 50000) || is_plus`
+ build the user instruction once for both templates (de-dup the 3 sites). Plus
model now emits REAL word timestamps (jfk json: {"text":"and","t0":33,"t1":59},
SRT splits 0.33/3.88/6.69/9.31 s matching parakeet) + speaker tags. The
text-splitter (rc1) still powers --max-len on non-plus granite/qwen3 (no word
timings). The "no spaces" issue is fixed by real word output. Lesson: garbage
LLM-ASR output that has right TIMING but wrong CONTENT = wrong chat template, not
a decode bug; compare the model card / ref blueprint prompt EXACTLY (incl. the
chat-template wrapper, not just the instruction text).

**#205c (main 0cb3d3d1) — blueprint byte-exact + other capabilities:** user pushed
'"thank you content" can NOT be correct, compare python blueprints'. Rendered the
REAL prompt via `transformers.apply_chat_template` on the actual HF tokenizer
(downloaded tokenizer only): the template ALWAYS prepends a default SYSTEM turn —
`<|start_of_role|>system<|end_of_role|>You are a helpful assistant. Please ensure
responses are professional, accurate, and safe.<|end_of_text|>\n<|start_of_role|>user<|end_of_role|><|audio|>{instr}<|end_of_text|>\n<|start_of_role|>assistant<|end_of_role|>`.
My v3 prefix started at the USER turn → added the system turn (both prefix sites)
→ now byte-exact. CONFIRMED via same tokenizer: granite-speech-4.1-2b BASE renders
`USER: <|audio|>X\n ASSISTANT:` (legacy!) so base/plus genuinely use DIFFERENT
templates → my is_plus→v3 discriminator is right, base stays legacy (correct).
Capability audit (model card): ASR✓ timestamps✓ SAA✓(diarize→"(speaker 0)")
AST/translate✓(both models, legacy ok) combined-SAA+ts FIXED (was leaking raw [T:N]
into text — SAA split returned early before ts parse; refactored [T:N] parse into
shared lambda threading mod-1000 rollover, applied per speaker turn). Japanese=base
only. **#205d (main 8fad1cb9) — KWB + incremental decoding NOW WIRED:** keyword biasing
= `--hotwords a,b,c` appends " Keywords: a,b,c" to ASR-family instruction (model
card KWB prompt; skip translate/--ask). Incremental decoding = new `--prefix-text
TEXT` seeds the assistant turn (`...assistant<|end_of_role|>{prefix_text}`) so
model CONTINUES from it; output = continuation only (validated: prefix "...ask not
what your country"→"can do for you..."). Both in transcribe() + streaming override
(also fixed streaming prompt builder which had DRIFTED to system-less user-only
prefix — brought up to #205c template). params.prefix_text in whisper_params.h.
Answered issue #205 on GitHub (comment). All granite capabilities now done.

**#205e (main 467f8052) — NO-SPACES root cause found + fixed:** reporter confirmed
--max-len works but plus text comes out word-concatenated ("ifyougotsomethingtosay").
ROOT CAUSE = the [T:N] parser's word capture `(\S+)` is GREEDY ACROSS the '['. Model
card spaces its pairs ("hello [T:45] world") and jfk parses fine, but on continuous
dialogue the plus model emits RUN-ON pairs with no spaces ("if[T:7962]you[T:7970]got")
→ \S+ swallows the whole run + embedded tags into ONE token → text loses all spaces.
FIX = capture word as `([^\[\s]+)` (non-space, non-'['); splits at bracket regardless
of spacing; simulation-verified spaced form byte-identical (no regression), run-on now
splits if/you/got. PENDING runtime confirm on reporter's 2.5min sample (SSD
/Volumes/backups detached; sample saved at issue205-sample/t32-first_2.5m.wav in repo
dir). Reporter's provided json was PRE-FIX (showed "ASSISTANT"/"050050" derailment =
the legacy-template bug already fixed). STILL OPEN: plus "misses a passage ~1:55" on
2.5min (completeness — likely a chunk derailing; model-card remedy = incremental
decoding wired into long-audio chunking, needs SSD to repro+verify). Lesson: \S+ in a
tag-stripping regex over-matches across the delimiter — use a negated class.

**#205f (main 8fd9db8f) — REAL no-spaces + missed-passage FIXED (reproduced!):**
auto-downloaded granite-plus-q4_k-MINI (1.66GB, registry granite-4.1-plus is q4_k
2.96GB; HF cstr/granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus-GGUF) since SSD detached; ran reporter's
2.5min wav (saved issue205-sample/, model models-test/granite-plus-mini.gguf in repo
dir). BOTH issues were in the CLI LONG-AUDIO path, NOT the model: (1) NO-SPACES =
crispasr_run.cpp chunk-context text REBUILD concatenates word.text with NO separator
(assumes whisper/parakeet leading-space convention); granite [T:]-words are BARE
("on") → "previouslyonmccloud's". FIX = insert space unless word starts with space OR
CJK boundary (preserves 617cd02 JA kana fix). #205e regex was necessary-not-sufficient
(parse_ts made right words, dispatcher re-joined spaceless). (2) MISSED-PASSAGE =
plus [T:] word timestamps DON'T align with overlap-save slice boundaries → word-level
trim drops most words (2.5min→36s text, gaps 30-80s/83-138s); base has no word-ts →
segment-level filter keeps all → "base did better". FIX = add "granite" to
crispasr_chunk_context_gate.h kBlocked (same as cohere/voxtral/qwen3 which had IDENTICAL
word-trim-drop); bare slices transcribe full, 1:55 passage recovered. +strip residual
"_ [T:179]". Validated: default -ojf spaced+full (666 vs base 524 vs broken 430);
751/751 tests. Posted fix to GitHub. Lesson: LLM-ASR with native word-ts + overlap-save
chunk trimming = dropped slices (the kBlocked list exists for exactly this). Lesson: to match an LLM chat prompt, RENDER it with the real tokenizer's
apply_chat_template — the system turn + exact control tokens matter, not just the
instruction text.

Validated M1/Metal jfk.wav: non-plus granite/qwen3 --max-len 30/25 → clean ≤N-char
SRT (were unsplit); plus -osrt --max-len + --output-json-full → correct text (were
"thank you" loops); parakeet --max-len still word-timed (no regression); 746/746
unit tests (UPDATED tests/test_diarized_json.cpp:120 which pinned the OLD
no-split-without-words behaviour = the bug). Open: granite-plus native word
timestamps still broken (model/prompt issue, gated opt-in for future fix).

## #221 irodori voice cloning SHIPPED (agent memory `project_221_irodori_voice_cloning`, migrated 2026-08-06)

---

description: Irodori-TTS

Irodori-TTS (#221) three follow-ups from bakamomi, all shipped to main 2026-07-07:

1. **Emoji → single token / noise** = tokenizer, TWO fixes.
   (a) 6029a51a: `core_spm::tokenize` collapsed to just BOS on any OOV multibyte
   codepoint (utf8_aligned single-byte unk fallback i→i+1 illegal at a multibyte
   lead, i+1 = continuation byte skipped by the guard → no edge leaves i). Added
   codepoint-level unk fallback.
   (b) c5a69fc9 — the REAL fix: OOV emoji must use **SentencePiece byte_fallback**,
   not <unk>. llm-jp-3 emits OOV bytes as "<0xHH>" tokens (👂 → <0xF0><0x9F><0x91>
   <0x82>; 😮‍💨 = 😮 bytes + ZWJ(in-vocab id 29279) + 💨 bytes) and the model
   learned those byte sequences AS the emoji emotion controls. <unk> played them
   as noise. Added `core_spm::Config::byte_fallback` (256-entry byte→"<0xHH>" id
   table); irodori builds it from vocab at load. C++ tokens now byte-for-byte ==
   HF llm-jp-3 (verified: whisper line = same 47 ids). No GGUF change (byte tokens
   already in vocab). 😭/🥺 are single in-vocab tokens; 👂/😮‍💨 are byte-fallback.
   Emoji list: Irodori-TTS repo EMOJI_ANNOTATIONS.md / duration.py ALLOWED_ANNOTATION_EMOJIS.
   Other core_spm consumers (m2m100/indextts/parler/pocket_tts) don't set byte_fallback → unchanged.

2. **Remove spoken warning** = `--no-spoken-disclaimer` already existed (audible
   AI-disclosure prefix, prepended when `--voice *.wav` used; triggers on the
   `.wav` extension regardless of whether cloning took effect).

3. **Voice cloning** = ported the DAC-VAE ENCODER → real zero-shot cloning
   (6fec8338). Was a stub (only decoder was ported). See below.

#### Voice-cloning port (the hard part)

DAC-VAE = `Aratako/Semantic-DACVAE-Japanese-32dim` (pip `dacvae`, weights.pth 430MB).
Deterministic encode (irodori_tts/codec.py `encode_waveform`):
`mono → resample 48k → LUFS -16 normalize (audiotools BS.1770) → reflect-pad to
hop(1920) → encoder → quantizer.in_proj(z).chunk(2)[0] = mean → (T,32)`.
Irodori config: latent_dim=32, latent_patch_size=1, speaker_patch_size=1,
speaker_dim=768 → the (T,32) latent feeds `set_reference_latent` DIRECTLY (no patchify).

Encoder = 30 convs, all NormConv1d pad_mode="none" (symmetric pad (k-stride)*dil//2
baked into the Conv1d, NOT valid convs — stride-1 = SAME/identity skips) + Snake1d
(`x + sin(αx)²/α`). 4 EncoderBlocks (rates [2,8,10,12]): 3 ResidualUnits (dil 1,3,9)
→ Snake → strided downsample (k=2s, stride s, pad s/2). Reused core_dac::conv1d/snake.

TWO hardcoded blockers in synthesize (both were "unconditional" defaults that
IGNORED the reference — fixing the encoder alone was not enough):
- speaker state hardwired to zeros (never ran the speaker encoder);
- DiT attn_mask ALWAYS -inf on speaker positions. Added `attend_speaker` flag.

Validation (M1 Metal, q8_0 model + f16 codec): encoder latent cos=0.99996 vs
PyTorch GT; LUFS within 0.04 of audiotools; speaker sim to ref 0.079(baseline)→
0.637(clone) vs 0.702 for the official clone_gen1.wav (~91% of reference); ASR
roundtrip intelligible. Speaker CFG (cfg_scale_speaker=5.0) NOT yet implemented —
would close the 0.637→0.702 gap (potential follow-up).

#### SHIPPED (all deployed 2026-07-07)

- 4 commits on main: 6029a51a (tokenizer), d4b052fd (CLI wiring), 6fec8338
  (encoder → cloning), c1b9becf (speaker CFG). Issue answered twice.
- Encoder-enabled `cstr/irodori-tts-GGUF/dacvae-ja-32dim-f16.gguf` UPLOADED
  (196MB, was 141 decoder-only; 91 enc + 139 dec tensors, has_encoder=True,
  strict superset → safe drop-in). Users must re-download the codec.
- HF token is in `../.env` (i.e. /Users/christianstrobele/code/.env: HF_TOKEN,
  also GH_TOKEN, KAGGLE_API_TOKEN). `hf` CLI not persistently logged in — export
  HF_TOKEN from that file. Xet commit hung at 100% → pkill + re-run resumed from
  cache and committed 0-new-bytes (see `feedback_hf_xet_hang`).
- Speaker CFG (c1b9becf): independent-mode `v = v_cond + cfg_text*(..) +
  cfg_speaker*(v_cond - v_spk_uncond)`, spk_uncond = attend_speaker=false;

## #231 cohere-arabic loop = corrupt GGUF (agent memory `project_231_cohere_arabic_corrupt_gguf`, migrated 2026-08-06)

---
name: project-231-cohere-arabic-corrupt-gguf
description: "#231 cohere-arabic repetition loop was a CORRUPT GGUF (bad download zeroed encoder layers 20/24), not a runtime bug; fixed by re-download+reconvert; full GGUF set + imatrix + ref uploaded"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 4607143b-84cf-48f7-a5d4-2864e0a4b9dd
---

**#231 cohere-transcribe-arabic loop = corrupt weights, NOT a runtime/structural
C++ bug.** A bad download zero-filled byte ranges in the source
`model.safetensors`, leaving **encoder layers 20 & 24 with all-zero LayerNorm
weights** (+ half-loaded `attn.k.weight`). Their `out_norm` collapsed the
residual to exactly 0 → downstream diverged → decoder fell into the `🎵`/EOS-less
loop. The file was byte-complete (`complete=True`) but internally zeroed — size
checks don't catch it; scan tensor norms (`GGUFReader` → `np.linalg.norm==0`).

**The handover's premises were ALL wrong in the same way** (it's on the FIXED
branch now, commit d6bf998f/f04ba79f): the "bf16 torch reference loop" was *also*
the corrupt weights (the reference backend loads the same safetensors) — the
fresh-model bf16 reference generates correct Arabic. `drop_last_frame`, the
`▁` decoder-start prompt, and NeMo masked-subsampling were red herrings. Kept the
two genuinely-correct fixes (`drop_last_frame=false`→T_enc=139 matches oracle;
prepend decoder_start `▁`=13764 matching reference `decoder_input_ids`); reverted
all the masking (a no-op for single-utterance; valid_enc==T, no overhang).

**How found:** dumped per-stage encoder activations from CrispASR
(`CRISPASR_COHERE_DUMP_STAGES=<dir>`, env-gated, shipped) AND from transcribe.cpp
(the ggml oracle; `TRANSCRIBE_DUMP_DIR`, +`-DTRANSCRIBE_ENABLE_VALIDATION_HOOKS=ON`
and patch encoder.cpp/model.cpp to dump all 48 blocks). Bisected: blocks 0-19
cos 0.999, **block 20 = cos 0** (exactly zero). transcribe.cpp is the right
oracle — it beats the degraded torch reference.

**BENCHMARK METHODOLOGY (important):** crispasr **already matches** transcribe.cpp
(interleaved: total 1465ms vs 1477ms on 11s clip; enc 1055/1060, dec 407/410 on
M1 Metal). A first naive **sequential** benchmark showed "23% slower" — that was
pure **thermal-throttle noise**. ALWAYS interleave configs round-robin (M,O,M,O…)
and take median/min, never sequential blocks. An encoder flash-attn rewrite
(BD-as-F16-mask, gated `CRISPASR_COHERE_ENC_FLASH`) LOST the A/B (1103 vs 1017ms)
→ reverted; manual rel-pos attention is already competitive on M1.

**Shipped to HF `cstr/cohere-transcribe-arabic-07-2026-GGUF`** (new repo): f16,
q8_0, q4_k, q4_k-imatrix, the reusable `.imatrix.gguf`, `-ref.gguf` (crispasr-diff),
README. imatrix corpus = 48 CC0 Common Voice Arabic clips (`fsicoli/common_voice_17_0`
`ar/dev` tar); imatrix q4_k transcript-identical to plain q4_k (payoff only at
q3_k/iq4). Source re-downloaded to `/mnt/volume1/cohere-fresh` (CIFS
`/mnt/akademie_storage` was the corruption vector — download to local disk).

**-ref.gguf env gotcha:** `cohere_asr` needs **transformers-from-source (5.14+)**
(4.57 rejects it even w/ trust_remote_code). tf-5.14 hard-imports torchaudio →
on VPS torch 2.9.1 the base torchaudio `.so` mismatched → OSError; fix =
`pip install torchaudio==2.9.1` in a `--system-site-packages` venv. VPS ref dump
= bf16 (fp32 OOMs 7GB). See `feedback-storage-paths`, `reference-nemo-macos-reference`.

qwen3-tts code_pred perf (#245, PLAN §232) — DONE, on main: feature `a750a05e`, Kaggle kernel `15f0b601`, default flip `bf74d22b` (2026-07-11).

- **Fusing the 15 code_pred steps into one graph is impossible bit-identically**: top_k/seeded-RNG sampling runs on CPU between steps and picks the next codec_embd row → CPU logits round-trip per step is mandatory. Make dispatches cheap instead.
- **`QWEN3_TTS_CP_DIRECT`** — T=2 step-0 + T=1 step graphs (O15 topology), gallocr-allocated ONCE on the code_pred backend, dispatched sched-free. **Default ON on GPU backends, OFF on CPU** (`c->backend != c->backend_cpu`), env wins both ways.
- **Validation (all WAV md5-identical):** Metal 0.6B (12+ runs, GPU md5 61dc3746…, CPU md5 ba0c9d47…); CUDA P100 Kaggle kernel `chr1s4/crispasr-qwen3-cp-direct-cuda` 25.4→22.5 ms/frame (−11%), ASR verbatim; 1.7B-CustomVoice Q8_0 (mtp-fused per-step path) md5 ed6bb9c3… both ways.
- **Perf truth:** Metal idle ≈ equal (110 vs 111 ms/frame); Metal loaded ~3× faster (the SCHED path degrades badly under contention — that's the real win); **CPU 2× SLOWER** (87→160 ms/frame — per-step lm_head slot blit ~2.2 MB memcpy ×14/frame dominates) → CPU default stays OFF; rescue idea: 14 per-cb cached graphs or in-graph lm_head get_rows.
- **LK_BUCKET segfaulted on unmodified main** (sched-plan reuse, nil-buffer Metal inputs); reworked to per-bucket gallocr sched-free — fixed, md5-identical, stays OPT-IN (~10% slower Metal short outputs; fastest config on CUDA 21.4 ms/frame).
- **O15=1 no longer crashes on CUDA P100** (#56 was Jetson sm_87) — O15 is largely superseded by CP_DIRECT.
- **Generalizable pattern**: ANY "cached sched plan, skip reset/alloc" reuse is broken on current ggml (Metal nil buffers, CUDA assert). Fix: build graph once in own arena, `ggml_gallocr_new(default_buft(backend))` + alloc once, per step tensor_set + `ggml_backend_graph_compute` — single backend, no sched. Guard with per-node `ggml_backend_supports_op` + KV-buffer-placement check, fall back to sched. See the dev guide (`crispasr-crispembed-dev.md`), `project-ggml-sched-cross-backend-resolution`.
- **Talker step PROFILED + CLOSED (26757908):** `CRISPASR_METAL_PROFILE` on the 1068-node step graph → encode 2-3 ms, **GPU-execute 38-42 ms** — execution-bound; sched-free/ICB can't help (bucket 56 vs dynamic 54 ms/step confirms). ~460 real ops/step, mul_mat only 24%, ~85 conts/step; kernel COUNT is the ceiling, amplified by desktop-GPU time-slicing (identical 193-node graphs swing 4-17 ms gpu_us under WindowServer load). kv_self_attn node-slimming = shared 30-backend helper, DEPRIORITIZED.
- **Codec FASTCONV SHIPPED (8b12de6a→main 3584fac0, default ON, opt-out `QWEN3_TTS_CODEC_FASTCONV=0`):** `QWEN3_TTS_CODEC_TRACE` showed the 3-4s codec wall was waste, not conv math — (a) K=1 convs im2col'd (pure copy, ~300MB F32 intermediates, 75ms ×12 sites) → now direct channel matmul on [C,T]; (b) causal `ggml_pad_ext` landed on CPU (Metal rejects asymmetric PAD) → pad-inside-im2col + crop-first-T (voxcpm2 causal_conv1d_ggml trick); (c) fork's ggml_conv_1d casts F16 kernels→F32 in EVERY graph (~70ms in_conv) → F32 kernels baked at load (+55MB). Codec 3.9→1.3s Metal (md5-identical), 9.1→4.3s CPU (1 int16 LSB, PCM cos 1.0). Pipeline RTF 2.9→1.25. Remaining codec cost = legit K=7 SEANet im2cols.
- **CUDA defaults validated (kernel v2 → main 1b53e7be):** shipped CP_DIRECT+FASTCONV vs full-legacy on P100 — rc=0, PCM cos 0.9999999997 (md5 drift = K=1-matmul realization class, same as CPU), ASR verbatim, AR 24.7→22.3 ms/frame, wall 6.9→5.6s; direct and direct+LK byte-identical.
- **16GB-Mac 1.7B codec jetsam FIXED in practice (c74121b5):** post-FASTCONV, 1.7B-CV 156-frame output decodes rc=0 with DEFAULT chunking at ~6GB free (died pre-FASTCONV). CHUNK=48 works but non-default ctx → different conv warm-up at chunk boundaries → WAV not byte-equal (pre-existing chunked property).
- **§232 fully closed except:** Kaggle competitor RTF benchmark (predict-woo/qwentts.cpp) — unrun, needs user go-ahead (GPU quota + third-party builds).
- Gotcha: 0.6B voicepack (d=1024) passed to 1.7B talker (d=2048) → OOB assert in build_icl_prefill_embeds; 1.7B validation vehicle = 1.7B-CustomVoice baked speakers (no voicepack, no ICL).

#### §235 next-perf triage (PLAN b73b1763, 2026-07-11)
- **DEAD END — DON'T port Parakeet/Nemotron transducer decoder to GPU.** PLAN §232 lists it top (decode is host cblas_sgemv/sgemm, paper 12-19x) but a parallel session already measured batched/GPU decode **5-9x SLOWER** (d0bb4601/3fcd5ff3). Tiny per-step matmul + host↔device sync = where CPU cblas wins (same class as CP_DIRECT-on-CPU). Leave cblas decoder.
- **Moonshine encoder OWNED by parallel session** (worktree moonshine-decode-stash @46127dab; im2col of k≈127 conv1 over 176K samples). Hands off.
- **qwen3-tts talker** GPU-execution-bound (§232), not a target.
- **Pocket-TTS backbone KV cache — MEASURED, NOT WORTH IT (main 434b1883; timers d895e581; worktree removed).** The O(T²) host KV re-upload in `backbone_forward_step_ggml` is real but the constant is tiny. M1 Metal 71-frame synthesis (POCKET_TTS_BENCH=1): synthesize 4780ms; voice mimi-encode 2721ms (57%, cacheable §224); AR loop backbone **587ms (8.27/frame, 12%)** vs flow **1228ms (17.29/frame, 26%)**; mimi_decode 1003ms (21%). Backbone→0 ceiling is 12%, realistically ~7% for a risky attention rewrite → NOT justified. Measurement gate did its job (= vibevoice 0%-win lesson). Flow-net diffusion is the biggest repeatable AR lever but no cheap+safe win; deprioritized. Landed the useful backbone/flow timers only.
- **CosyVoice3 HiFT/FASTCONV — MEASURED, NOT WORTH IT (main d2ca57c1).** Downloaded full CV3 GGUF set → /Volumes/backups/ai/crispasr-gguf. COSYVOICE3_BENCH split (174-mel, M1): flow_euler 3526ms(48%), lm_ar_decode 2681ms(36%), hift_vocoder 1152ms(16%). HiFT 16% but FASTCONV barely applies: already uses pad-in-im2col (cv3_causal_conv1d); decode is SINGLE sched graph so F32-bake casts once (~15-20ms not per-frame); istft twiddle ~20-30ms; no K=1 convs (kernels 16/11/7). Addressable ~0.6% of 7.4s wall → fails A/B bar. Real costs = CFM diffusion + Qwen2-0.5B AR (compute-bound, no cheap conv win). PERFORMANCE.md "O(n²)→FFT" was WRONG framing (n_fft=16).
- **CosyVoice3 CFM flow-steps — CHARACTERIZED, recommend 10→6 (main 10696821).** flow_euler=48% of wall; COSYVOICE3_FLOW_STEPS already a knob (default 10). Swept 10/8/6/4 (--seed 42 = same LM tokens+noise). Quality=**log-mel corr vs 10-step** (ASR verbatim at 8/6, useless): 8→0.9948, 6→0.9925, 4→0.9895. **6=sweet spot** (≥0.98, ASR verbatim, matches chatterbox §207), ~−40% flow/~−19% wall; 4 = one-word ASR slip (localized artifact corr averages out). RECOMMENDED not flipped (quality default needs human listen). **CONFIRMED across diverse sentences (2ac74b0a):** 6-vs-10 mel-corr short/nums/long = 0.9953/0.9930/0.9938, ASR@6 verbatim on short+long (nums inconclusive — moonshine garbles digits at both). Recommendation now robust, only remaining gate = human listen. LEARNINGS: grade CFM steps w/ log-mel NOT ASR; calibrate metric to threshold (raw log-STFT read 0.958 falsely vs log-mel 0.9948 same audio); whole-utterance corr under-weights local artifacts.
- **CV3 default FLIPPED 10→6 (main b30082e5), user-listen-approved.** `flow_steps = min(cfm_n_steps, 6)` at synth dispatch (hp.cfm_n_steps=10 preserved for diff harness). Validated: default synth == explicit-6 (mel-corr 1.0000), vs 10-step 0.9925. ~−19% CV3 wall. COSYVOICE3_FLOW_STEPS overrides.
- **§235 outcome:** pocket-tts + CV3-HiFT-FASTCONV = NOT-WORTH-IT (FASTCONV/CP_DIRECT were qwen3-tts-specific: K=1-im2col + per-chunk casts; other vocoders already pad-in-im2col + single-graph). CV3 flow-steps = the ONE actionable win, SHIPPED (10→6). Runtime-perf vein mined; rest owned (CUDA-graph transducer, Moonshine) or algorithmic. Measurement gate killed 2/3 speculative targets before building.
- **POCKET-TTS ONSET GONG (user-caught, LOCALIZED, fix-decision OPEN):** every pocket-tts synthesis opens with a decaying ~1kHz transient at t=0 (RMS 0.070→0.007 over ~0.4s) BEFORE speech — ASR + peak/RMS gates ALL missed it, only human listen caught it (= vibevoice onset-artifact class). **Localized via POCKET_DUMP_DIR trace:** first generated LATENT frame is 1.23× hot (L2 6.78 vs median 5.52), codec AMPLIFIES it (mimi upsample frame0 1.68×) → audible pre-speech gong. **Key context:** default synth auto-voice-conditions on samples/jfk.wav (138-frame prefill) then generates — the gong is the generation cold-start after that prefill (hot first latent + codec causal-conv empty left-context). **FADE WAS A BAND-AID (user rejected it) — REAL ROOT CAUSE FOUND via reference diff (aaa3bcb8 fade default-on should be REVERTED).** Set up reference env: /Volumes/backups/ai/pocket-ref-venv (moshi 0.2.13 + `pip install pocket-tts` + gated model, HF_TOKEN from ~/.cache/huggingface/token, `logged in as cstr`; model at /Volumes/backups/ai/huggingface-hub/hub/models--kyutai--pocket-tts 209M). WAV voice cloning is GATED — needs HF auth (works). Reference script tools/reference_backends/pocket_tts_reference.py has an API-compat KV-init bug on the voice path; bypass with the high-level API: `state=m.get_state_for_audio_prompt(wav); m.generate_audio(state,text)` + forward-pre-hook on m.flow_lm.flow_net to capture backbone_out.
**DECISIVE FINDINGS:** (1) kyutai model is HIGH-QUALITY (web: not a documented problem) → OUR bug. (2) no-voice output CLEAN (first latent 2.79 ≈ ref 2.82); WITH jfk voice = gong. (3) **CODEC IS CORRECT** — force-decoding the REFERENCE's exact latents through OUR codec (POCKET_FORCE_LATENTS) gives the SAME clean quiet onset (t0=0.0045) as the reference; force-decoding OUR latents gongs (t0=0.0621). Same codec path → LATENTS are the diff, not the codec. (4) Our latents ≈ ref (frame0 corr 0.949) but the ~32% L2 diff (dims 29/22/28...) is enough — the codec onset is sensitive. (5) First-frame backbone_out corr only **0.877** vs ref (12% off) → systematically wrong. (6) **ALL seeds gong** (1/7/42/123) → SYSTEMATIC, not sampling. (7) Tensors (bos_before_voice L2=0.5853, bos_emb L2=0.1656) byte-identical; prefill order [bos_before_voice,voice,text,gen] matches; decoder-only self-attn architecture matches. **CONCLUSION: subtle numerical divergence in our VOICE-CONDITIONING prefill → systematically-wrong first-frame backbone output (0.877) → wrong first latent → codec renders gong. NOT YET FIXED — needs diffing voice-prefill KV/positions/attention to close 0.877→1.0.** Incidental: POCKET_FORCE_LATENTS SIGSEGV fixed (KV-size before init).

## #249 MOSS-Local 4B stop-runaway = PROMPT tokenization bug (agent memory `project_249_moss_local_prompt_tokenization_bug`, migrated 2026-08-06)

---
name: project_249_moss_local_prompt_tokenization_bug
description: "MOSS-TTS-Local 4B stop-runaway was a PROMPT-tokenization bug (non-compositional BPE), NOT the forward; check input-token parity before blaming numerics"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3461be21-6490-43c0-99f8-d002c91784ab
  modified: 2026-07-28T09:02:23.420Z
---

#249 MOSS-TTS-Local 4B binary stop head ran away (q6_k/q8_0 always, q4_k coin-flip). ROOT CAUSE (fixed on main 1a5c352a, 2026-07-28): `mtl_generate_grid` built the whole generation prompt as ONE string and tokenized it in a single `moss_tts_local_tokenize` call. BPE is non-compositional (`encode(A+B) ≠ encode(A)+encode(B)` at merges), so the user text embedded in the `…- Text:\n{text}\n</user_inst>…` template drifted **~2 tokens** vs the HF reference processor, which encodes each segment separately + splices special-token ids directly. FIX: piece-wise assembly mirroring `processing_moss_tts.py` (encode `"user\n"`, `"<user_inst>\n- Reference(s):\n"`, `"None"`, fields block, text ALONE, `"\n</user_inst>"`, `"\n"`, `"assistant\n"` each separately; im_start/im_end/audio_start as literal ids). Validated on Kaggle: channel-0 ids == reference `input_ids` exactly (62/62, 69/69); q4_k + f16 both stop 4/4 at 11–39 frames. So q6_k/q8_0 now shippable.

**Why:** the last prompt token is `<audio_start>` (special, tokenizes correctly either way) so last-position Q/K was byte-exact — hid the bug. The interior mis-tokenized tokens are weighted ~0 by early attention but AMPLIFIED by the layer-10 attention sink → backbone hidden drifts (cos 0.99998@blk9 → 0.9996@blk10 → 0.991@35) → stop gap stays high → runaway. Every forward check passed (f16≡f32 GGUF byte-identical, flash_attn_ext≡numpy-eager cos 1.0, ggml_rope≡HF half-split, KV-cache+GQA preserve K to 1e-7, eager-F32 attn byte-identical to flash on CPU since GGML_PREC_F32 is a CPU no-op) — the forward was correct; the INPUT tokens were wrong. I wrongly concluded "irreducible ggml-vs-torch f32 accumulation / ship q4_k only" and burned ~a dozen Kaggle builds first.

**How to apply:** When a from-scratch port's forward diverges from a reference but EVERY discrete op is machine-precision-correct with an exact input, the bug is in the INPUT, not the forward — diff the FULL input-token grid vs the reference processor (not just the last position: specials tokenize fine, interior text drifts). And diff against a SECOND independent working port — here `github.com/mudler/moss-tts.cpp` (its own code comments named this exact "big-string encode drifts ~2 tokens" bug) + the OpenMOSS llama.cpp fork; a fork-agent file-by-file comparison pinned it. A reference's own emphasis is a clue: the HF README said "the tokenized generation prompt matches the reference processor exactly … so the model stops where it should." Diagnostic envs in `moss_tts_local.cpp`: `CRISPASR_MOSS_TTS_LOCAL_{DUMP_STOP,DUMP_LAYERS,DUMP_SUBLAYER,DUMP_PROMPT_IDS,FORCE_FRAMES,GREEDY_TEXT}`; eager-F32 attn via `CRISPASR_CORE_ATTN_EAGER_F32=1` (GPU-only benefit). See the dev guide (`crispasr-crispembed-dev.md`), the dev guide (`crispasr-crispembed-dev.md`).

---
name: project_249_moss_voice_cloning_shipped
description: "MOSS-TTS-Local voice cloning shipped and Kaggle-validated (sim gain +0.33, WER 0.0); reference rows are NOT delay-shifted; the spoken disclaimer contaminates any clone measurement"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 985745b9-3527-4757-b6c4-a432453387ac
  modified: 2026-08-01T16:14:11.241Z
---

MOSS-TTS-Local (#249) voice cloning is **shipped and validated** (3a6ec094 +
71992e56). Kaggle acceptance run: sim(baseline, ref) 0.5402 → sim(cloned, ref)
**0.8700**, gain +0.3299, `wer_cloned` **0.0** (verbatim). Kernel
`tools/kaggle/moss-clone-accept`.

#### The load-bearing blueprint detail

Reference rows are **NOT delay-shifted**.
`processing_moss_tts.py::_build_audio_rows` writes the codes straight into
columns 1..n_vq under the USER slot token; only *generation* is delayed. The
older MOSS-TTS-v1.5 STUDY.md says "splice delay-shifted ref codes", which is
about the other model — following it here would smear the reference across n_vq
frames. Codes are `(n_vq, T)` row-major our side, `[T, n_vq]` in the reference.

Requires the encoder-carrying codec `moss-tts-local-v1.5-codec-enc.gguf`; the
plain `-codec.gguf` is decode-only and degrades to the default voice with a
warning.

#### Any clone measurement must suppress the spoken disclaimer

Cloned output gets an audible "This audio was generated by artificial
intelligence" prefix that the non-cloned baseline does **not**. It spoke in a
different voice (polluting speaker similarity) and added nine words the ASR
faithfully transcribed — first run read `wer_cloned` 0.3889 vs 0.1111 baseline on
output that was otherwise verbatim, i.e. it looked like a regression and was an
artefact of the comparison. Use `--no-spoken-disclaimer
--accept-marking-responsibility`; the inaudible watermark and C2PA stay on.

Also: **resemblyzer must be pinned to CPU on Kaggle** — the P100 is sm_60 and
the installed torch wheel has no kernels for it ("no kernel image is available"),
which silently killed the entire similarity leg.

Related: `project_310_cosyvoice3_zeroshot_leak` (why the reference transcript
is deliberately not the synthesized text), the dev guide (`crispasr-crispembed-dev.md`),
the dev guide (`crispasr-crispembed-dev.md`).

#299 (base 1.5B/7B + `vibevoice-voice-*.gguf` realtime pack → static) FIXED (3f26d7a0) and now RUNTIME-REPRODUCED on M1 Metal, q4_k.

**Repro (both arms):** A) base + realtime pack → guard fires (`the 1.5B/7B base model cannot use realtime voice packs`), `TTS synthesis failed`, no WAV written. B) base + `--voice jfk.wav --i-have-rights` → WAV route runs (`voice ref encoded: 83 frames`, `prompt 132 tokens (83 voice frames)`) → intelligible speech (tiny-ASR roundtrip: "this is a test of" verbatim; the appended AI disclaimer, same model/voice, transcribes cleanly; signal healthy all quarters). Backend alias `vibevoice-tts` and `vibevoice-1.5b` both hit the shared `vibevoice_synthesize` guard (line ~3241, quant-independent).

**Why the pack can't be reused by the base model (inspected the pack GGUF):** `vibevoice-voice-*.gguf` contains ONLY KV-cache tensors — `voice.lm.{N}.{k,v}`=[64,132,2], `voice.tts_lm.{N}.{k,v}`=[64,309,2], neg=[64,1,2]. No raw audio, no VAE latents. Three blockers: (1) geometry — pack KV `head_dim=64` (realtime-0.5B) vs 1.5B base `head_dim=128` (d_lm 1536/12), different layer count → `copy_voice_kv` needs matching ne[0..2], fails; (2) `tts_lm` KV targets a head the base lacks (`tts_n_layers=0` = is_base_model); (3) base conditions by PREPENDING acoustic+semantic VAE frames encoded from a raw waveform (`at_enc`/`st_enc` → connector), NOT by KV injection like realtime — no lossless KV→frames transform. To ever make base+pack work you'd regenerate packs embedding the SOURCE reference audio/latents; can't recover from KV-only packs. See `project_vibevoice_quant_music_intro_171`.

**Local-repro gotchas:** base.en/large-v3-turbo in `~/crispasr-live-cache` are symlinks to the `/Volumes/backups` SSD which the agent process CANNOT read (Operation not permitted) — use `~/code/gguf-models/ggml-tiny.bin` (real 77MB) for roundtrips. Disk was ~3GB free; downloaded 1.9GB q4_k, repro'd, deleted. Pre-existing `build/bin/crispasr` was a thin CLI loading `libcrispasr.1.dylib` — grep the dylib (not the 2.7MB binary) for a guard string; the stale-.o trap: force-touch the src if an incremental build doesn't pick up a committed fix.

never sets `seg.speaker`. VibeVoice's speaker info is INLINE TEXT the model
writes — literally `[{"STart":0,"End":6.67,"SPeaker":0,"Content":"..."}]` — so
#300 is a **no-op for vibevoice** (that text already flowed through streaming).
To know if #300 helps a backend, grep its adapter for `.speaker =`, don't trust
the cap. Backends that DO set structured `seg.speaker`: **moss-diarize** (parses
`[Sxx]`→`"(Speaker N) "`, adapter line 77), **granite** in speaker-aware
`--diarize`/SAA mode, and the file-mode `crispasr_diarize_cli.cpp` /
`tiron_link.cpp` post-processing (offline only). See `project_299_vibevoice_1p5b_pack_incompatible`.

#308 (bilo1967): `--backend whisper --output-srt` → first word double-capitalised
("Hello"→"HEllo") + a full stop appended to every cue. ROOT CAUSE: `--backend
whisper` uses the DISPATCH path (crispasr_run.cpp), whose
`crispasr_should_auto_enable_punctuation` (crispasr_punctuation_policy.h)
auto-runs FireRedPunc on any backend lacking `CAP_PUNCTUATION_NATIVE` /
`CAP_PUNCTUATION_TOGGLE`. The whisper adapter (crispasr_backend_crispasr.cpp
capabilities()) declared NEITHER → FireRedPunc ran a 2nd pass on whisper's
already-cased+punctuated text. (Default no-`--backend` path = historical cli.cpp,
never post-punctuated — so only explicit `--backend whisper` hit it.)

VERIFIED end-to-end on Kaggle (chr1str/crispasr-whisper-punctuation-308-verify,
CPU build of main): `--backend whisper` on jfk.wav → "And so my fellow Americans..."
(single cap, no trailing full stop) and BYTE-IDENTICAL to the no-`--backend`
historical path. Kernel gotcha: whisper prints "[ts] text" — must extract text
AFTER the "]" (v1 filtered those out → false empty-transcript FAIL).

TWO fixes (pushed cfbc082e, main):
1. Add `CAP_PUNCTUATION_NATIVE` to the whisper adapter caps → policy skips it.
2. FireRedPunc rule capitaliser (fireredpunc.cpp ~838) only cleared `cap_next`
   when up-casing a LOWERCASE letter; an already-uppercase first letter left the
   flag set → next letter up-cased too. Now clears `cap_next` on any A-Z emit.
   Proven by isolated sim: "Hello"→"Hello", " the cat. hi."→" The cat. Hi."

⚠ FOLLOW-UP AUDIT (open): any OTHER ASR backend that natively punctuates but
declares neither NATIVE nor TOGGLE gets the same wrong 2nd pass (fix #2 stops the
double-cap for them, but a spurious period would remain). Grep each ASR adapter's
capabilities() for CAP_PUNCTUATION_NATIVE. Could not build/roundtrip locally
(loadavg ~28 + internal disk 100% full) — CI compiled it; run the real
`--backend whisper --output-srt` roundtrip when the box frees. See
`feedback_no_concurrent_heavy_crispasr_m1`.
